Raspberry Pi based computer offers Real-Time Ethernet

Can someone give a basic explanation what "real-time ethernet" is? And how is it different from regular ethernet? The article is very technical, and googling it produced similarly complicated results.

Regular ethernet has something called collision time that presents a time delay on ethernet between command and execution of that command.Thats not very good for delicate stuff like robotics,where delays measured in microseconds matter.

So they receive the signal with the Pi process it and then relay it again on to the device as a way to reduce delay. That seems counter intuitive, normally to remove delay you would want less between the machinery and the system sending commands not add more. If this can be done with such simple hardware why not have it built into the system and avoid the extra relay step.
Its just the idiot in me thinking,but im pretty sure it has something to do with spying capability.

Modem Ethernet doors not use a shared bus. It uses a point-to-point connection between each device and an Ethernet switch. The switch stores packets and then resends them only to the necessary destination ports.

"Real time" just means that the engineers designed everything so that data is delivered in a small, predictable amount of time. It takes a lot of attention to detail to make this work. Most computers designs are pretty casual about delays, which is why they are prone to random pauses. But you can't have random pauses if you are running sensitive machinery.
